title: Redis versus a local cache
context: Why use Redis instead of a local in-process cache?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Redis questions (1 of 2)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: A local cache, such as Caffeine, is the fastest option, with no network hop. But each server has its own copy, so the copies can disagree and each one warms up separately. Redis is one shared cache. Every instance sees the same data and invalidation applies everywhere. The cost is a network round trip and an extra system to run. Many systems use both: a small local cache in front of Redis.

points.title: Consistency across instances
points.why: Local caches diverge across servers, and Redis keeps one copy.

points.title: Network cost
points.why: Each Redis read is a network round trip, which local memory avoids.
